- relates to https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/8456
- relates to https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/14835


This field indicates whether a repository is an official image (Docker Library / Docker Official Images). This information is deducted from the image reference, and not used anywhere, other than in tests.

The `RepositoryInfo` and `IndexInfo` types were originally introduced in 568f86eb186731b907b659e4ec64bda21c2fe31d, with their fields documented in 4fcb9ac40ce33c4d6e08d5669af6be5e076e2574.

At the time, the `Official` field was only used for `docker push` to produce a custom error message if someone would attempt to push an official image to docker hub (assuming nobody would be able to do so); https://github.com/moby/moby/blob/6870bde5847d4484d87f91baf58edc52f575ea5d/api/client/commands.go#L1184-L1194

Before that commit, the condition for this error message was based on the given image reference directly; b370acd679622239849b1dfbe05d61804aeb7162 https://github.com/moby/moby/blob/b370acd679622239849b1dfbe05d61804aeb7162/commands.go#L421-L428

This patch deprecates the field, because it's not used, and removes tests related to it.

body:
### 🎯 Goal The default padding (`safeDrawingPadding`) applied to the stateful `MessageComposer(MessageComposerViewModel)` could add undesired padding when used in app which targets SDK 35 and is running on a device on Android 15 or above. This is because the `safeDrawingPadding` applies the `systemBars` padding (top and bottom) + `ime` padding (bottom). If a parent component already applies this padding and the insets are not consumed, this padding will be applied twice. Additionally, this padding is not applied to the stateless `MessageComposer(MessageComposerState)` components, so the behaviour between the stateful and the stateless types of the `MessageComposer` is different. With this PR, the `safeDrawingPadding` is removed to be unified with the stateless `MessageComposer`, and to prevent double appliance of the padding. (`MessagesScreen` will not be affected, as the root component there already applies the `safeDrawingPadding` in the parent component). ### 🛠 Implementation details - Remove `safeDrawingPadding` from stateful `MessageComposer(MessageComposerViewModel)` component - Remove unnecessary elevation in `AttachmentsPicker` - Update `Configuration.sampleTargetSdk` to `35` - Update sample apps to support `EdgeToEdge` for demo purposes ### 🎨 UI Changes
Compose XML
### 🧪 Testing 1. Run compose/xml sample apps on device running Android 15 2. Enter a channel 3. Type a message 4. None of the screens/components should be cut of by the system insets (status bar, nav bar, ime...)

author: sisidovski
body: This will address the comment in https://github.com/whatwg/fetch/pull/1737#issuecomment-2385734506. When "race-network-request" is matched as the router rule, the service worker starts a network request in parallel with dispatching the fetch event. The response is keyed by request and managed in [race response map](https://w3c.github.io/ServiceWorker/#serviceworkerglobalscope-race-response-map). And the fetch API will check this map whether the request is already started by the service worker, and use its response if the corresponding entry is found. We use [ok-status](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#ok-status) to tell if the response is successful or not, and use the response only when the status is ok-status. This is needed to support the offline capability. However, with the request mode "no-cors", the response will be [filtered](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-filtered-response-opaque). The filtered response's status is always 0, so this is handled as a failure in "race-network-request" even without this change. But it would be better that we explicitly filter out "no-cors" in the handle fetch algorithm. Once we get an agreement to this change, I'll add a WPT and fix Chrome behavior. *** Preview | Diff

body:
Resolve phase 1 of issue #111 

After extensive reading about Supabase, what makes supabase attractive is it's built-in user authentication system. We can use the built-in authentication systems to validate user logins, sign-ups, sessions, and instances without building it all from scratch. With this PR, I focus on adding a basic auth layer to our app.

# Features
- Supabase client is used to handle authentication
- User can use the signup page to create a new account
- Once the account is created, the user can sign in using the newly created email and password provided. 

# Testing
1. Create a [supabase project](https://supabase.com/dashboard/projects)
2. Get the generated URL and Anon keys: Supabase dashboard -> Project settings -> Data API (under configuration tab)
![CleanShot 2025-03-03 at 00 56 37](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d68d625d-1708-48b2-aa29-72956a675a71)
3. Save the credentials to an .[env file](https://github.com/SeattleColleges/shift-app-expo/blob/experiment-auth-implementation/.env.sample)
4. [Copy, paste](https://github.com/SeattleColleges/shift-app-expo/blob/experiment-auth-implementation/supabase/snippets/profile.txt), and run the SQL code in the Supabase dashboard SQL editor
![CleanShot 2025-03-03 at 01 01 59](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d717ada9-2222-43cc-9f9e-80458efe6394)
5. Run `npm install`
6. Create an iOS or Android instance w/ `npm run start`
7. Use the app's signup page to create a new user account. You should be automatically directed to the main app page. 
8. Log in using the newly created user credentials on the login page. An alert will provide authentication credential details. 
9. Pat yourself on the back for successfully getting this far 🎉🎈

There will be a PR soon adding a local instance of Supabase, which will allow us to have our local instance to build with. Reach out if you have any issues.

---------

The 8.3.0 release failed to include the change notes and docs for the release. This patch release remedies this. There are no other changes.
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 8.3.0
   ```
   =========================

New features
------------

- `12231 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/12231>`_: Added `--xfail-tb` flag, which turns on traceback output for XFAIL results.

  * If the `--xfail-tb` flag is not given, tracebacks for XFAIL results are NOT shown.
  * The style of traceback for XFAIL is set with `--tb`, and can be `auto|long|short|line|native|no`.
  * Note: Even if you have `--xfail-tb` set, you won't see them if `--tb=no`.

  Some history:

  With pytest 8.0, `-rx` or `-ra` would not only turn on summary reports for xfail, but also report the tracebacks for xfail results. This caused issues with some projects that utilize xfail, but don't want to see all of the xfail tracebacks.

  This change detaches xfail tracebacks from `-rx`, and now we turn on xfail tracebacks with `--xfail-tb`. With this, the default `-rx`/ `-ra` behavior is identical to pre-8.0 with respect to xfail tracebacks. While this is a behavior change, it brings default behavior back to pre-8.0.0 behavior, which ultimately was considered the better course of action.

  -- by :user:`okken`


- `12281 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/12281>`_: Added support for keyword matching in marker expressions.

  Now tests can be selected by marker keyword arguments.
  Supported values are :class:`int`, (unescaped) :class:`str`, :class:`bool` & :data:`None`.

  See :ref:`marker examples <marker_keyword_expression_example>` for more information.

  -- by :user:`lovetheguitar`


- `12567 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/12567>`_: Added ``--no-fold-skipped`` command line option.

  If this option is set, then skipped tests in short summary are no longer grouped

  way as other statuses.

body: Hi Boas, I added a checkpoint which checks the mean coverage from wgs metrics file and creates flags. The delly rule is then run according to if the flag states 'low' or 'sufficient'. Low is any mean coverage < 1 (this was a test threshold because I noticed the samples that were failing were below this but we can choose a better one based on more testing. I also use the checkpoint in variant_filtering.smk rule filter_large_deletions as this rule depends on the output of delly. If the coverage is flagged as low, i have for now just created empty files because the delly tool does not seem to have a (clear) option of dealing with the low cov samples.
